_comment: Barbaro activation template for Claude Code. Copy these entries into
~/.claude/settings.json (or a project .claude/settings.json) and replace
BARBARO_BIN with the absolute path to the installed `barbaro` binary.
These installed hooks stay dormant for every new session until the user
invokes the project skill with `/barbaro`. Mentioning that command
elsewhere does not opt in. Joined sessions write derived copies
of their traces into
<project>/.barbaro/, which may be shared or committed. Add `.barbaro/`
to .gitignore first unless the project has decided to publish it.
Every command is fail-open. If the binary is missing, errors, or is slow,
the coding turn proceeds unaffected — an advisory lease and a derived
digest are never worth failing real work over.
After a session joins, two commands perform two jobs:
`claude hook`        keeps the present-tense activity lease current.
`claude hook-ingest` publishes completed turns and child bundles.
Why ingestion runs on more than Stop: a subagent launched with
status async_launched is only attested complete once the parent records
its task notification, which can land AFTER the parent's own Stop.
The ingest handlers are asynchronous except SessionEnd, so they never
delay the event whose trace record they may be waiting for. SubagentStop
polls for the correlated completion record; SessionStart, TaskCompleted,
UserPromptSubmit and SessionEnd provide bounded catch-up sweeps.
